issues.description: `Seen.ref` and `Seen.parent` lack a written contract distinguishing their roles
issues.detail: Two fields now carry overlapping meaning: `ref` (processor-set inheritance source) and `parent` (clone-chain ancestor), with the rule `if (!result.ref) result.ref = parent`. The invariants — when ref==parent, when they diverge, what each guarantees to `flattenRef` — are nowhere stated. SPEC-MISSING. Without a docblock describing the two-field contract, future maintainers will re-confuse them. Write the contract on the `Seen` interface.

issues.description: `flattenRef` silently mutates `seen.ref` to null as recursion guard, conflating 'unset' with 'already-flattened'
issues.detail: The sentinel `seen.ref === null` means 'already processed' while `undefined` means 'never had one'. Callers reading `Seen.ref` post-finalize cannot distinguish these states. LEAKY-ABSTRACTION: an internal recursion guard leaks into the field's domain. Introduce a separate `flattened: boolean` flag or a local visited set so `ref`'s type stays honest.

issues.description: Property de-duplication via `JSON.stringify` equality is an unstated, fragile contract
issues.detail: Two passes delete keys when `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])`. This silently assumes key-order stability, no undefined values, no Dates/functions, and structural (not referential) equality semantics. The ADT here is 'JSON Schema fragment equality' — it deserves a named helper with a stated contract, not stringify-as-equals scattered in two places.

issues.description: Removal of `if (!seen.isParent)` guard around `ctx.override` weakens an existing postcondition
issues.detail: Previously `override` was invoked only for non-parent nodes; the test `overrideCount` doubling 6 -> 12 confirms a behavior change for user-supplied overrides. This is an LSP-style contract weakening of `ctx.override`'s call frequency. Either document this as the new contract (parents are now overridable) and call it out in changelog, or restore the guard. Silent doubling will surprise downstream override authors.

issues.description: `isParentRef` check via `(zodSchema as any)._zod.parent === ref` re-derives state that `Seen` already tracks
issues.detail: `flattenRef` already has `seen.parent` available, but reaches back into `zodSchema._zod.parent` with an `any` cast to decide branch behavior. The module boundary is being crossed for information the local Seen record should already carry. Compare `seen.parent === ref` instead, and lift the `any` cast — the type of `_zod.parent` should be expressed on the schema interface.

issues.description: `play.ts` switched from package import to deep relative source path
issues.detail: `play.ts` now imports `./packages/zod/src/index.js` instead of `zod/v4`. This is a scratchpad change that shouldn't ship in the PR — it couples a top-level playground file to internal source layout and will break for anyone consuming the repo via the published entry. Revert before merge.

review.summary: The patch adds a useful distinction between processor-set `ref` and clone-chain `parent`, fixing a real bug for wrapper schemas with ids. But the new two-field contract on `Seen` is not written down anywhere, and the implementation leans on stringify-equality and `any` casts to compensate. The override-guard removal silently doubles user override invocations — a contract change that needs to be either reverted or declared. Tighten the spec on `Seen`, extract a named JSON-fragment-equality helper, and decide deliberately about the override semantics before merge.
